chapter: Queens Terrace, Decca records and Amen
title: Recording day before the USO tour and the Amen affidavit
summary: He leaves for Fort Lewis the day he records, has a bandmate sign, and later gets an affidavit that he did Amen.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I only agreed to go out for the camp shows, USO camp shows. The day I recorded, on October 21, 1941, I went immediately-- there were some friends of mine who will be at the party tonight, Bo Bueteau--

Yeah, and Tibby Bibby. They were taking me out to dinner because I had to catch a plane at eight o'clock that night to go out to Fort Lewis, Washington, and so Mayo said come here and sign this now, but we didn't think it was going to be anything, we made (inaudible). So I told Reese, he was one of the boys, a Tampa Boy, I said sign it for me Reese and he didn't think it was going to be any-
thing, and we just went on off, because there was a little (inaudible) waiting for me, in the studio.
Some groupie, they had groupies back then too.
But I even got an affidavit from Reese that I was the one that did "Amen".
It would be helpful to have that.
You should have an affidavit; sure, why not. Mayo shouldn't be allowed to take that--
Yeah, they told me he's dead.
